I have farmed these 16 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. I never went to school — everything I know, I learned by doing and watching my neighbors. My old lady and me are the only ones at home now, so I hire machines for the heavy work and get day-laborers when we need extra hands.

For winter wheat, I plant the same improved seed Old Wang used last year, about 15 kg per mu. At planting time I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, then when the wheat greens up I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, and another half bag when it joints. I know that is a lot of white fertilizer, but two years ago I tried to save money and used less, and the wheat turned yellow and thin. I lost nearly 100 kg per mu. Never again. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate four times: winter water after the seed is in, jointing, heading, and once more in May if the rain stays away. I spray three times — herbicide in spring, then bug medicine when the heads come out. I rotary-till before planting. If the weather is normal, I will get about 520 kg per mu.

For summer corn, there is no time to plow after cutting wheat — the season is too short. I plant hybrid seed right away with the no-till machine, about 2.5 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer down with the planter, about half a bag per mu, then side-dress with half a bag of urea when the corn is knee-high. I irrigate three times: after sowing if the ground is dry, at the big flare stage, and when the ears fill. I spray three times for weeds and the corn borer. I expect about 600 kg per mu. That is what my neighbors get, so that is what I aim for.
